items.title: Kidd Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006
items.q: I had a set of fingerings that worked for me when I was in high school with all of that. I just worked them out.

ctx.x: Rascher, Sigurd Rascher, and somebody named Nash. I had a set of fingerings that worked for me when I was in high school with all of that. I just worked them out. I just had a system, I just was hearing high. And I went on. Then when I got to college they wouldn’t let me play saxophone ‘cause it wasn’t a classical instrument, you had to play clarinet. And that broke my heart. And you know what I had to do in order to stop playing it? I took all the pads out of my saxophone. I still got that. I took all the pads…

you know so I could have some extra change. But I got to be a senior and then I was back on my saxophone because I felt like I could, you know I wouldn’t have to spend all that time on the saxophone. Because I knew if I had it working then I wasn’t going to practice the clarinet.
